item.title: Volatile eutectics to tailor crystallization for perovskite optoelectronics
item.description: Improvements to the radiative efficiency of halide perovskite thin films are necessary to approach fundamental solar cell performance limits. We tailored perovskite crystallization by leveraging the eutectic interaction between zinc bromide and methylammonium chloride additives. The resulting films had high photoluminescence quantum yield and charge carrier decay times and low surface recombination velocity. Nanoprobe x-ray microscopy revealed local melting of the eutectic at grain boundaries...

item.title: Artificial intelligence-based thigh muscle volume profiling on CT in elderly East Asian patients with hip fracture
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Elderly hip fracture patients exhibited a dissociation between muscle quantity and quality. The relatively high fatty degeneration observed in stabilizing muscles, including the gluteal muscles and multifidus, despite their large volume, may reflect muscle composition patterns potentially related to postural function. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospective studies incorporating direct functional assessments.

item.title: Room-Temperature Selectivity Switching via Nanoporous Au Film-Integrated SnO<sub>2</sub> Hybrid Sensors
item.description: Metal oxide chemiresistive sensors operating at room temperature offer a promising route toward low-power gas monitoring, but their selectivity remains largely governed by the intrinsic surface chemistry of the oxide. Here, we report a transport-engineered Au nanoporous metal film (Au NPMF)-integrated tin dioxide (SnO(2)) hybrid structure (Au NPMF@SnO(2)) that reverses the native sensing preference of SnO(2) at room temperature. A continuous Au NPMF is conformally integrated with...

item.description: The radial electric field (Er) is important for turbulence suppression and transport barrier formation in magnetically confined plasmas. To establish the diagnostic capability required for its future determination, the Korea Superconducting Tokamak Advanced Research (KSTAR) Motional Stark Effect Background Polychromator was modified to measure the polarization angles of the full-energy π and half-energy σ Stark components simultaneously along a common line of sight (LOS). item.title: Degradation of (S)-1,3-butanediol in Pseudomonas putida KT2440 reveals a CoA-activation route and enantiomeric crosstalk between (R)- and (S)-3-hydroxybutyrate catabolism
item.description: 1,3-Butanediol (1,3-BDO) exists as (R)- and (S)-enantiomers, yet how aerobic bacteria catabolize the (S)-form has been unknown. Here, we define (S)-1,3-BDO degradation pathway in Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and uncover an enantioselective enzyme that both controls the pathway and enables a chiral resolution. Transcriptomics, quantitative RT-PCR, and systematic gene deletions show that the ped cluster oxidizes (S)-1,3-BDO to (S)-3-hydroxybutyrate [(S)-3-HB] using the same upstream machinery as...

item.title: High-Mobility Chalcogenophene-Engineered Diketopyrrolopyrrole Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conductors With Doping Tolerance for Low-Power Organic Electrochemical Transistors
item.description: Optimizing the steady-state performance of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) requires simultaneous control over both molecular-level design and structural ordering in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Here, we report a series of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based polymers functionalized with aliphatic-glycol hybrid side chains (PDPP-4EG-T2 and PDPP-4EG-Se2) and systematically investigate the impact of their structure on OECT performance. item.title: A nuclear ERK-ATF5 axis coordinates mitochondrial metabolism and thermogenic gene expression in brown adipocytes
item.description: Obesity and diabetes arise from disrupted energy homeostasis, underscoring the need to identify mechanisms that enhance energy expenditure. Brown adipose tissue dissipates energy through mitochondria-dependent non-shivering thermogenesis; however, the transcriptional regulators coordinating this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated the role of activating transcription factor 5 in thermogenic programming and mitochondrial metabolism in brown adipocytes using in vivo and in...

item.title: Suppressing Stitching Errors in Full-Sensor-Plane Color Routers via Optical Structural Similarity
item.description: Nanophotonic color routers promise higher photon utilization than absorptive color filters for complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors, yet most reported designs remain optimized for normal incidence, with efficiency dropping to about half of its peak by θ ≈ 6 ° . Here, we present an angle-specific inverse-design framework in which the sensor plane is partitioned into local angular zones, and each zone is assigned a dedicated color-router unit cell. To enable practical...

item.title: Pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila as a candidate multi-effector pharmacological system in the gut-liver axis: evidence, unresolved causality, and translational priorities
item.description: Pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila is a clinically tractable postbiotic candidate, but its activity cannot be assigned to a single principle. Heat-stable Amuc_1100 is demonstrably retained in pasteurized cells, whereas the GLP-1-inducing protein P9, extracellular vesicles (AmEVs), membrane lipids, and diffusible metabolites are supported mainly by studies of live bacteria or isolated preparations, whose retention and activity in pasteurized products remain unestablished; together they create...

item.title: All-in-One Multispectral Stealth Device for X-Band Radar, Visible, and Near-Infrared Spectra
item.description: Multispectral stealth is a critical technology in modern military and security applications. Conventional approaches generally address stealth in only one or two spectral bands-such as radar, visible light, or infrared (IR)-thereby limiting their effectiveness against advanced detection systems. In this study, we present, for the first time, an integrated and dynamically adaptive electrochromic system capable of achieving simultaneous stealth across the radar, near-infrared (NIR), and visible...

item.title: Robust Generation of Topological Biphoton Mode via Adiabatic Passage
item.description: Topological waveguide arrays support robust mode propagation in the presence of fabrication imperfections, providing a significant advantage for on-chip quantum information processing. However, this robustness does not fully extend to nonlinear biphoton generation. Structural disorder can enhance the excitation of nontopological biphoton modes during nonlinear interactions, which degrades the quantum properties of the generated state. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adiabatic passage...

item.title: Development of a Lensless Compact Optical System for Ultrasensitive Nanomaterial Detection in Liquid Media via Exploiting Multiple Light Scattering
item.description: Accurate detection of nanoparticles in liquids is essential across drug delivery, diagnostics, and environmental monitoring. Dynamic light scattering (DLS), the current gold-standard technique, relies on single-scattering events and requires prior knowledge of sample temperature and optical properties, limiting its sensitivity at low particle concentrations and increasing system cost and complexity. Here, we present a lensless, cost-effective speckle-based method that exploits multiple light...

item.title: Tunable Photonic Applications Based on Electrochemical Mechanisms
item.description: Reflective displays offer key advantages such as high energy efficiency, eye comfort, and excellent visibility, making them attractive for a wide range of applications. Recently, tunable photonics has focused on integrating electrochromic (EC) materials with optical resonant structures, enabling dynamic control of reflection spectra and intensity through enhanced light-matter interaction. Here, this review provides an overview of recent progress in electrochemically driven dynamic coloration...

item.title: Predatory Mechanisms of Myxobacteria and Their Potential in the Development of Biocontrol Agents
item.description: Climate change, environmental degradation, and the depletion of finite resources are intensifying the search for sustainable, bio-based solutions across agriculture, environmental management, and chemical production. Against this backdrop, myxobacteria have emerged as a valuable but still underused microbial resource, distinguished by their ecological versatility, multicellular behavior, predatory lifestyle, and biosynthetic capacity. This review integrates the mechanistic basis of myxobacterial...

item.title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

item.title: Morphological, Molecular Phylogenetic, and Mitochondrial Genome Characterization of a Deep-Branching Marine Flagellate, Katablepharis ulleungensis sp. nov. (Cryptista)
item.description: Katablepharids (or kathablepharids) are plastid-less, biflagellate protists widely distributed in marine and freshwater environments. Here, we report a new katablepharid species, Katablepharis ulleungensis sp. nov., isolated from a black sandy beach in Ulleung-do, South Korea. The stock strain was co-cultured with a small bicosoecid flagellate, serving as its prey. Cells were oblong, displayed two rows of Type I ejectisomes, and possessed two subapically inserted flagella with the posterior...

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development
item.description: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream...

item.title: Clarifying the Concept of "Unanticipated Transfer to the ICU": A Scoping Review
item.description: Unanticipated transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU), typically defined as an unscheduled escalation of care from inpatient general wards, is widely used in clinical research as a marker of adverse events, clinical deterioration, and system failure. However, its conceptual meaning, definition, and operationalization vary substantially across the literature, complicating interpretation and cross-study comparison. We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to map how...

item.title: RINGSIDE Phase II Study of Varegacestat for Treatment of Desmoid Tumors: A Randomized Dose-Finding Clinical Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Varegacestat demonstrated clinically meaningful DT volume reduction and ORR with a manageable safety profile across dose regimens. The largest responses were seen with the 1.2-mg once-daily dose, which was selected for the RINGSIDE phase III trial.

item.title: Accurate stock movement prediction via centroid-based randomness smoothing
item.description: How can we identify stable patterns to accurately predict stock price movements amidst severe market noise? Predicting stock price movements is a crucial problem in financial data mining, and has attracted significant attention from researchers and financial institutions. Although there have been several works on learning patterns from quantitative data to predict stock prices, they encounter critical challenges from data uncertainty and model limitations. Data uncertainty arises in financial...

item.title: Ensemble multi-retrieval methodologies with reasoning model decision in multi-step biomedical QA
item.description: Robust and trustworthy biomedical question answering (QA) remains a critical challenge for large language models (LLMs), especially in complex domains such as rare diseases, where information is fragmented across multiple sources. MedHopQA 2025 benchmark introduces 10 000 multi-step reasoning questions curated from Wikipedia, requiring systems to extract, connect, and synthesize biomedical knowledge across interlinked documents. In this work, we present a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and...

item.title: Maternal Influenza Infection During Pregnancy and Neuropsychiatric Disorders in Offspring
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this binational cohort study of mother-child pairs in South Korea and Japan, the modest population-level association between maternal influenza infection during pregnancy and the risk of any neuropsychiatric disorder in offspring was attenuated and not statistically significant in sibling-comparison analyses in either cohort. These findings suggest that familial factors may account for the association observed in the population-level analysis.

item.title: Comparative effects of maxillary total-arch distalization using Class II elastics alone vs miniscrew assistance in nonsurgical adult Class II correction: A retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In nonsurgical adult Class II correction, elastics primarily act on the mandibular dentition, whereas MTAD produces greater maxillary distalization and may reduce dependence on patient compliance.

item.title: NK2.2/Vnd acts as a transcriptional activator of deadpan to maintain neuroblast identity in Drosophila embryos
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that Vnd directly binds to a specific cis-regulatory motif within the dpn promoter, functioning as a transcriptional activator to maintain NB identity and architectural integrity during Drosophila embryogenesis.

item.title: Inhibition of adipocyte-macrophage interaction via CSF1-CSF1R by curcumin
item.description: Adipocytes (Ad), macrophages (Mac), and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in the adipose tissue (AT) of individuals with obesity may jointly contribute to obesity-induced pathogenesis. This study aims to examine the roles of adipocyte-macrophage interaction (AMI) and LPS in obesity-induced pathogenesis, as well as the effects of curcumin (Cur) on these interactions. An indirect co-culture model using conditioned media (CM) from 3T3-L1 Ad and J774A.1 Mac, with LPS, was used. AMI in AT and its association...

item.title: Duration of protective effect after benzathine penicillin G prophylaxis for recurrent cellulitis: a 14-day window of efficacy
item.description: CONCLUSION: The protective effect of intramuscular BPG against recurrent cellulitis was most pronounced during the first two weeks after administration, supporting the potential utility of individualized, shorter dosing intervals.

item.title: Tube-in-tube hollow RuCrMn oxide nanofibers for noble-metal-efficient oxygen evolution via Cr/Mn-regulated Ru active sites
item.description: Reducing the Ru content while maintaining high oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity remains a major challenge. In this study, single phase Ru(0.30)Cr(0.31)Mn(0.39)O(2) nanofibers were prepared through electrospinning process followed by temperature-regulated heat treatment. The temperature regulation process induces a unique formation of a hollow tube-in-tube structure while simultaneously influencing crystallinity and defect distribution. item.title: Improving predictive accuracy for surgical indication of the current management guideline for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm of the pancreas via cutoff adjustments
item.description: CONCLUSION: Current HRS criteria carry a high false-positive rate for malignancy. Increasing EMN and MPD cutoffs improves specificity and AUC, though sensitivity decreases. Thresholds should be optimized according to the clinical context.

item.title: Transient flow modulation with rapid-resorbable gelatin microspheres during Yttrium-90 radioembolization for liver cancer: a preliminary clinical trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: RGM-mediated flow modulation was associated with reduced Y-90 microsphere deposition in the NTL, with imaging findings suggesting regional liver function preservation. This protective effect appeared greater with lower Y-90 microsphere load.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Genomic-guided precision oncology in canine cancer: from comparative genomics to liquid biopsy and molecular monitoring
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Genomic-guided oncology offers substantial clinical value for canine cancer management yet requires veterinary-specific validation before broad adoption. Targeted sequencing panels currently represent the optimal balance of cost-effectiveness and clinical utility for most veterinary practitioners, while ddPCR is preferred for longitudinal tracking of known mutations. Liquid biopsy cannot serve as a standalone screening tool at present, but functions as a valuable...

item.title: iProDNet: integrated probabilistic differential network inference under heterogeneous biological conditions
item.description: Understanding phenotype-specific network rewiring is essential for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. Although numerous differential network analysis methods have been developed, most focus on only a limited aspect of network information. item.title: Causal decomposition framework for quantifying intervenable cancer health disparities
item.description: This study proposes a nonparametric decomposition framework to quantify and prioritize the impact of multiple intervenable mediators contributing to disparities in health outcomes. Identifying modifiable components of health disparities is essential for informing policy and guiding resource allocation, but several methodological challenges remain. item.title: Reaction-Specific Ultralow-Pt-Integrated CuCo Carbonate Hydroxide Nanoneedles for Durable Alkaline Seawater Electrolysis
item.description: Developing bifunctional electrocatalysts that combine high activity, low noble-metal usage, and durability in alkaline seawater-containing electrolytes is important for sustainable hydrogen production. Herein, Pt-integrated copper cobalt carbonate hydroxide nanoneedle arrays grown on Ni foam were prepared by hydrothermal synthesis followed by controlled Pt electrodeposition. item.title: Emergency Department Clinicians' Needs for User-Centered Antibiotic Guideline: Insights from a Focus Group Interview
item.description: CONCLUSION: ED clinicians perceived existing antibiotic guidelines as poorly aligned with ED practice. User-centered, institution-specific antibiotic guidelines may enhance applicability and support appropriate empirical antibiotic prescribing in the ED.

item.title: The Impact of a Hand Hygiene Education Program in Long-Term Care Facilities in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: In the multi-district study of 17 LTCFs, an in-person HH education program was associated with improved caregiver compliance. These findings support expanding and sustaining HH education across Korean LTCFs.

item.title: Clinical Characteristics of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Korean Children: An 11-Year Multicenter Retrospective Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: RSV infection in our cohort predominantly affected young infants, with a post-pandemic shift toward older age groups. The high proportion of full-term infants without underlying conditions among severe cases reflected cohort composition rather than enriched risk. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that broader prevention strategies covering all infants, alongside high-risk groups, warrant population-level evaluation.

item.title: Long-term Immunogenicity and Safety Profile of the Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccine in Korean Older Adults: A Sub-analysis of a Phase 3 Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: In Korean adults aged ≥60 years, a single dose of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine elicited a robust immune response, which persisted for up to 24 months post-vaccination, with an acceptable safety profile.

item.title: Clinical Practice Recommendations for the Treatment of Candida auris Infection in Korea
item.description: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen associated with invasive infections and high mortality. In Korea, C. auris infections have historically been caused predominantly by Clade II isolates; however, recent reports of invasive infections due to Clade I indicate an evolving epidemiology with potential implications for antifungal resistance and treatment strategies. To provide practical guidance for clinicians, we developed evidence-based recommendations for the...

item.title: Recommendations for Adult Pneumococcal Vaccination in Korea: 2026 Update Incorporating the 21-Valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine
item.description: The 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV21; CAPVAXIVE; Merck Sharp & Dohme) is the first pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) specifically designed for adults, targeting serotypes that currently cause disease in this population. PCV21 includes 11 serotypes not contained in any other approved PCV (9N, 15A, 15C, 16F, 17F, 20A, 23A, 23B, 24F, 31, and 35B), together with serotypes 3, 6A, 7F, 8, 10A, 11A, 12F, 19A, 22F, and 33F. PCV21 was approved by the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug...

item.title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Perspectives on Persistent HIV-1 Low-Level Viremia
item.description: While modern antiretroviral therapy achieves high rates of virologic suppression, persistent low-level viremia (pLLV) remains a common clinical scenario that poses distinct diagnostic and therapeutic dilemmas. This review proposes a systematic diagnostic approach to pLLV, beginning with a thorough evaluation of adherence, potential drug-drug interactions, dietary considerations, and resistance profiles. Such a structured assessment is essential to differentiate diverse pathophysiological...

item.title: Allelic Architecture and Clinical Spectrum of RP1-Associated Retinal Dystrophies in a Multicenter Korean Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This large ancestry-specific RP1-associated retinal dystrophy cohort refines the allelic landscape and underscores the importance of phasing and MEI-aware testing strategies, revealing broad phenotypic expansion to macular and cone(-rod) dystrophies and genotype-dependent severity profiles.

item.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Albuminuria in Diabetic Patients Using Retinal Microvascular Metrics on Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: OCTA parameters are significantly associated with albuminuria in diabetes, and their inclusion in predictive models improves albuminuria identification, supporting OCTA as a noninvasive complementary tool for early detection of DN.

item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurobiologically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, yet current treatment approaches - predominantly behavioral and communicative - pharmacological option limited to symptomatic relief, with limited benefit for individuals with more severe presentations. item.title: Electro-optical memristors: from the origin to device implementation
item.description: With the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, conventional von Neumann architectures face increasing limitations arising from memory-processor separation, high data-transfer latency, and power consumption. Memristive devices offer a promising route towards in-memory and neuromorphic computing by combining information storage and processing within compact two-terminal structures. item.title: Investigating Denosumab Interference in Serum Protein Electrophoresis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although denosumab exhibited a consistent electrophoretic migration pattern in vitro, it did not cause clinically relevant in vivo interference in SPEP or immunotyping assays. These findings support accurate electrophoretic interpretation and reduce concerns regarding misclassification of M-proteins in patients with MM receiving denosumab.

item.title: Angular and Spectral Engineering of Red Organic Light-Emitting Diodes via Cavity-Induced Emission for Photobiomodulation-Related Cellular Responses
item.description: Photobiomodulation using red and near-infrared light has emerged as a promising strategy for promoting skin regeneration because of its ability to stimulate mitochondrial activity and enhance cellular proliferation. However, the optical characteristics of the light source, including angular emission and spectral bandwidth, remain underexplored in terms of their influence on biological outcomes. Here, we demonstrate that emission-engineered red organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) can directly...

item.title: Sequential Versus Combined Liver-Kidney Transplantation in Pediatric Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1: A Multi-Center Comparative Cohort Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among pediatric patients with primary hyperoxaluria Type 1 who completed both liver and kidney transplantation, sequential transplantation was associated with favorable observed kidney graft outcomes. These findings describe outcomes among recipients who completed both procedures and should not be interpreted as outcomes of an initially intended sequential strategy.

item.title: To be (IIb), or not to be (IIb) - That is the current status of cuffless blood pressure monitoring device
item.description: Cuffless blood pressure (BP) monitoring devices have attracted extraordinary scientific and commercial attention, yet their clinical status remains deeply contested. item.title: Development of a predictive platform for target concentration intervention of aminoglycosides
item.description: Aminoglycosides, including gentamicin, are potent bactericidal antibiotics that are widely utilized for the treatment of severe gram-negative bacterial infections. These drugs demonstrate a concentration-dependent bactericidal effect, whereby higher concentrations result in more rapid bacterial elimination. item.title: LC-MS/MS quantification of N-lactoyl-phenylalanine and N-lactoyl-tyrosine in human plasma: method validation and clinical application to metformin administration
item.description: N-lactoyl amino acids, including N-lactoyl-phenylalanine (Lac-Phe) and N-lactoyl-tyrosine (Lac-Tyr), have recently attracted interest as endogenous metabolites of potential clinical and metabolic relevance. In particular, Lac-Phe has been implicated in appetite regulation and in the metabolic effects of metformin. item.title: Real-world performance of a ring-type cuffless blood pressure device compared with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory, real-world study found that CART BP pro-derived period summaries showed lower SBP values and smaller nocturnal BP declines than ABPM. Because period-level aggregates were compared rather than simultaneous point-to-point measurements, these findings should not be interpreted as a formal accuracy validation of the device. item.title: The evolving landscape of inflammation-related clinical trials: a 25-year registry-based network analysis from a clinical pharmacology perspective
item.description: The longitudinal evolution of inflammation-related clinical research has not been systematically characterized at the registry level, and the differential impact of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic across inflammatory disease domains remains incompletely resolved. We analyzed 15,051 inflammation-related interventional trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (2000-2025), stratified into pre-pandemic (≤ 2019; n = 10,366), pandemic (2020-2022; n = 2,356), and post-pandemic...

item.title: Case Report: Fournier's gangrene caused by Gleimia hominis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This case highlights the pathogenic potential of G. hominis in necrotizing soft tissue infection and the value of precise microbiologic identification for antimicrobial de-escalation.

item.title: Unveiling Search-Robust One-Shot Learning Operation in FeTFT-Based Ternary Content-Addressable Memory
item.description: With the rapid growth of data-centric artificial intelligence (AI), ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) has emerged as a promising platform for parallel in-memory search. Here, we systematically investigate how the gate-dielectric material and structural design of metal-ferroelectric-metal-insulator-semiconductor (MFMIS) ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) affect TCAM search operation and long-term robustness. item.title: Motility-mediated drug interactions with GLP-1 receptor agonists: labeled evidence and a framework for quantitative assessment
item.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely prescribed, and two additional oral products received US approval in 2025 and 2026. All eleven US labels examined describe delayed gastric emptying as potentially affecting the absorption of co-administered oral medications. Since the exenatide program, no study has evaluated a narrow therapeutic index victim across more than one administration schedule; the original warfarin and digoxin studies each used a single schedule. item.title: Cuffless 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring-guided antihypertensive titration in real-world clinical practice: a prospective non-randomized study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this non-randomized study, a care pathway incorporating cuffless 24-hour ABPM was associated with lower 24-hour ambulatory systolic BP at 6 months compared with usual care, whereas office systolic BP did not differ significantly between arms. Given the non-randomized design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in a randomized trial.

item.title: Dynamic One-Dimensional Beam Shaping via a Mechanically Tunable Bilayer Metasurface
item.description: Tunable metasurfaces have emerged as a promising platform for active wavefront control beyond the static functionality of conventional designs. Although mechanical actuation in bilayer metasurfaces offers large tuning ranges and robust operation, previous studies have predominantly focused on two-dimensional (2D) beam control that requires complex phase profiles and is subject to design constraints arising from the limited degrees of freedom available in two-axis modulation. item.title: One-Dimensional Acoustic Plasmons in Metallic Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
item.description: Acoustic plasmons, collective out-of-phase oscillations of image charges, can confine electric fields with exceptional strength, making them highly effective for applications requiring intense field localization. Here, we predict the existence of one-dimensional (1D) acoustic plasmons in metallic single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) on metallic substrates. These 1D acoustic plasmons achieve intensive electric field concentration with the plasmon wavelength contracted by approximately 22%...

item.title: Beyond population size: long-term changes in free-roaming cat population structure during TNR implementation in Seoul
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings describe population-structure patterns observed during implementation of Seoul's public TNR program, including reduced kitten counts and increased neutering probability over time. Given the observational nature of the study and the absence of untreated controls, these findings cannot demonstrate the causal effects of TNR. Nevertheless, structural indicators may complement simple procedure counts to identify sites requiring further intervention in urban cat management.

item.title: Disorder-Enabled Directional Delocalization and Wave Steering in Time-Modulated Dirac Materials
item.description: We demonstrate a disorder-enabled yet localization-immune directional transport channel in time-modulated Dirac systems subject to stochastic temporal variations of a vector potential. In a spatially uniform medium, random temporal modulation induces strong Anderson localization for generic propagation directions, whereas waves propagating parallel to the modulation axis remain perfectly delocalized. item.title: A Deterministic Spectral-Design Method for Guided-Mode Resonances
item.description: Resonance frequency and linewidth are key metrics for guided-mode resonance (GMR) devices and their independent control is important for practical applications. Trial-solution-based approaches have been used to obtain appropriate element designs with desired key metrics. In this paper, we propose a dual-ridge compound unit-cell structure for fully independent key-metric control in a deterministic manner. item.title: Comparative hepatic safety between tegoprazan and esomeprazole: a real-world cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Tegoprazan was associated with fewer laboratory-defined hepatic events than esomeprazole in this dataset. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation using standardized monitoring and adjudicated outcomes.

item.title: Delayed Postoperative Malignant Hyperthermia After Total Intravenous Anesthesia: A Case Report
item.description: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare pharmacogenetic disorder typically triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine, but its occurrence after total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) remains exceptional and underreported. Propofol-based TIVA is recommended for MH-susceptible patients to avoid known triggers, yet absolute prevention cannot be guaranteed. A 24-year-old male with prior suspected MH underwent spine surgery under propofol-remifentanil TIVA after strict preventive preparation....

item.title: An external peer review instrument for Korean Medicine clinical practice guideline drafts (KM-EPRI): development and content validation
item.description: CONCLUSION: KM-EPRI can serve as a consensus-based, structured reference for the external peer review of KM-CPG drafts during development. Its effect on review quality and inter-rater reliability remains to be evaluated in practice.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Hallux valgus is highly prevalent in patients with femoral neck fracture and is independently associated with lower postoperative motor function. Assessment of hallux valgus may provide additional insight into postoperative functional prognosis in this population.

However, it faces technical challenges when applied to beam-sensitive samples or agglomerated nanoparticles. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The SRD demonstrated favourable clinical usability and acceptability compared with the CSE, particularly from the clinician's perspective, while patient-reported outcomes were largely comparable between the two devices. item.title: Clinicians' Trust in AI-Based Clinical Recommendations Across Controlled Primary Care-Style Clinical Vignettes: Nurse-Dominant Experimental Pilot Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported trust differentiated correct from incorrect recommendations in aggregate, while acceptance and rejection were not fully aligned with recommendation correctness. These preliminary findings identify a potential evaluation problem: lower trust in incorrect advice does not necessarily imply that users will reject it. The findings do not establish real-world clinical effects.

item.title: An eco-evolutionary consumer-resource theory of host-microbe symbioses
item.description: Symbiotic associations between microorganisms and hosts are universal, diverse, and dynamic. Yet, our ability to represent this complexity mathematically remains limited. We propose extending consumer-resource theory to incorporate evolutionary processes to advance our understanding of symbioses, from pairwise interactions to complex host-microbe assemblages. item.title: eHealth-Guided Exercise Improves Peak Oxygen Uptake and Health-Related Quality of Life After COVID-19: A Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A six-month eHealth-guided exercise intervention using AQ was more effective than standard PA advice in improving V̇O2peak and mental HRQoL among physically inactive adults recovering from COVID-19. These findings highlight the potential of AQ as an effective and feasible approach for post-COVID rehabilitation.
